Republic–Georgia–Italy–Germany]]|}} }} '''Daniel Theis''' ({{IPAc-en|t|aɪ|s}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=24 October 2023|access-date=17 May 2024}} born 4 April 1992) is a German professional [[basketball]] player for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. After seven seasons in the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] where he was a four-time All Star and three-time [[List of German basketball champions|champion]], Theis signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] of the NBA where he played for four seasons before a trade brought him to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in March 2021. The Bulls traded Theis to the [[Houston Rockets]] in August 2021, who in turn traded Theis back to the Celtics in February 2022, before being traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in July 2022. He reached the [[NBA Finals]] during his second stint with the Celtics. ==Early life== Born in [[Salzgitter]],{{Cite web |title=Daniel Theis Biography - ESPN (AU) |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/player/bio/_/id/2451037/daniel-theis |access-date=2025-08-11 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=August 2025}} Theis went through the [[Basketball Löwen Braunschweig|Braunschweig]] youth system.{{Cite web |title=Die Nachwuchsarbeit und die Partner – Basketball Löwen Braunschweig |url=https://www.basketball-loewen.de/nachwuchs/die-nachwuchsarbeit-und-die-partner/ |access-date=2025-08-11 |website=www.basketball-loewen.de}} ==Professional career== ===Phantoms Braunschweig (2010–2012)=== Theis made his debut in the [[German basketball league system|German top-tier level league]], the [[Basketball Bundesliga]], during the [[2010–11 Basketball Bundesliga|2010–11 season]]. Theis primarily gained playing time with [[Basketball Löwen Braunschweig|Braunschweig]]'s development squad, where he played alongside his older brother, Frank,{{Cite web|date=5 November 2009|title=Daniel Theis für U18-Nationalmannschaftskader nominiert|trans-title=Daniel Theis nominated to U18 national team|url=http://www.basketball-loewen.de/presse/news/einzelner-beitrag/article/daniel-theis-fuer-u18-nationalmannschaftskader-nominiert.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621115859/https://www.basketball-loewen.de/presse/news/einzelner-beitrag/article/daniel-theis-fuer-u18-nationalmannschaftskader-nominiert.html|archive-date=21 June 2018|access-date=2 July 2017|website=Basketball Löwen Braunschweig|language=de}} from 2010 to 2012. He earned the ''[[Eurobasket.com]]'' website's All-2.[[Pro B]] Most Improved Player of the Year honors in 2011. In Braunschweig, Theis was also a teammate of fellow future NBA player [[Dennis Schröder]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketball-loewen.de/presse/news/einzelner-beitrag/article/dennis-schroeder-ist-youngster-des-jahres-in-der-prob.html|title=Dennis Schröder ist "Youngster des Jahres" in der [[Boston Celtics]] re-acquired Theis from the Rockets in exchange for [[Bruno Fernando]], [[Enes Freedom]], and [[Dennis Schröder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-re-acquire-daniel-theis-0|title=Celtics Re-Acquire Daniel Theis in Four-Player Deal with Rockets|publisher=National Basketball NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], but lost to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 6 games. ===Indiana Pacers (2022–2023)=== On 9 July 2022, Theis was traded, alongside [[Nik Stauskas]], [[Aaron Nesmith]], [[Malik Fitts]], [[Juwan Morgan]] and a 2023 first-round pick, to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Malcolm Brogdon]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Announce Trade With Boston knee surgery, Theis made his Pacers debut against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite magazine|first=Tony|last=East|title=Daniel Theis debuts for Indiana Pacers, shows how he can help|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/news/daniel-theis-debuts-for-indiana-pacers-shows-how-he-can-help|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=6 February 2023|access-date=6 February 2023}} On 13 February against the [[Utah Jazz]], Theis recorded a season–high 11 points, five rebounds, and three assists as the Pacers' starting [[Center (basketball)|center]].{{cite magazine|first=Tony|last=East|title=Daniel Theis receiving less playing time as Indiana Pacers look to develop young players|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/news/daniel-theis-receiving-less-playing-time-as-indiana-pacers-look-to-develop-young-players|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=8 March 2023|access-date=8 March 2023}} Theis spent his [[2022–23 Indiana Pacers season|first season in Indiana]] as a mentor and backup to [[Myles Turner]], [[Jalen Smith]], and [[Isaiah Jackson (basketball)|Isaiah Jackson]] before falling out of the Pacers rotation. On 15 November 2023, Theis reached a buyout agreement with Indiana after seeing minimal action to start the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|2023–24 Pacers season]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Waive Daniel Theis|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-daniel-theis|website=NBA.com|date=15 November 2023|access-date=15 November 2023}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2023–2024)=== On 17 November 2023, Theis signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|title=LA Clippers Sign Daniel Theis|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-sign-daniel-theis|website=NBA.com|date=17 November 2023|access-date=17 November 2023}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2024–2025)=== On 9 July 2024, Theis signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign Daniel Theis|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/daniel-theis-center-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-2024-nba-free-agency-signing|website=NBA.com|date=9 July 2024|access-date=9 July 2024}} On 5 February 2025, Theis was traded alongside a 2031 second-round pick to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{cite web |title=Thunder Acquires Daniel Theis and 2031 Second Round Draft Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-theis-250205 |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 6, 2025 |date=February 5, 2025}} The next day, he was waived by the Thunder.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/okc-thunder-waive-daniel-theis-202343546.html|title=OKC Thunder waive Daniel Theis to open up 15th roster spot|work=Yahoo! Sports|date=February 6, 2025|first=Clemente|last= Almanza}} ===AS Monaco (2025–2026)=== On 17 February 2025, [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]] announced that Theis had inked a contract for the rest of the 2024–25 season and for the following campaign.{{Cite web |date=2025-02-17 |title=Daniel Theis, un champion du monde arrive en Principauté |url=https://asmonaco.basketball/news/show.php?ID=63211 |access-date=2025-02-17 |website=AS Monaco |language=fr}} During his stint with Monaco, he helped the team secure the [[2025–26 LNB Élite season|2026 LNB Élite championship]], the [[French Basketball Cup]] title, and the [[LNB Pro A Leaders Cup|French League Cup]]. ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2026–present)=== On 5 August 2026, Theis signed a two-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Maccabi makes marquee move for Daniel Theis|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/maccabi-makes-marquee-move-for-daniel-theis/|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|date=August 5, 2026|accessdate=August 5, 2026}} ==National team career== Theis was a member of the junior national teams of Germany. With the [[Germany men's national under-20 basketball team|Germany U20 national team]], he played at the [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2011 FIBA U20 European Championship]], and the [[2012 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2012 FIBA U20 European Championship]].{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis 2011 FIBA U20 European Championship statistics|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/281-fiba-u20-eurobasket/6390/players/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=24 July 2011}}{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis 2012 FIBA U20 European Championship statistics|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/281-fiba-u20-eurobasket/6787/players/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=22 July 2012}} [[File:20160903 Basketball AUT vs GER 8886.jpg|thumb|Theis with the Germany national team in a EuroBasket 2017 qualifier in 2016.]] On 27 July 2014, Theis made his first appearance with the senior [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany national team]] in a game against [[Finland men's national basketball team|Finland]].[http://mahr.sb-vision.de/dbb/html/herren/spieler/spielespieler.aspx?spnr=275 Daniel Theis profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150625193455/http://mahr.sb-vision.de/dbb/html/herren/spieler/spielespieler.aspx?spnr=275 |date=25 June 2015 }}. SB-Vision.de With Germany's senior team, he played in the [[EuroBasket 2015 qualification|EuroBasket 2015 qualification tournament]].{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis EuroBasket 2015 qualifiers statistics|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/205-fiba-eurobasket-qualifiers/7258/players/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=27 August 2014}} Two years later, Theis was selected to represent Germany at the [[EuroBasket 2017]], where he averaged 10.9 points and 6.3 rebounds per game during the competition.{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis EuroBasket 2017 profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/208-fiba-eurobasket/9604/players/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=12 September 2017}} At the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]], Theis finished the event with averages of 7.6 points and 6 rebounds per game.{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis 2019 FIBA World Cup profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/201-fiba-basketball-world-cup/9472/players/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=9 September 2019}} Heading toward [[EuroBasket 2022]], Theis helped Germany win bronze during the tournament, finishing with 8.8 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game.{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis EuroBasket 2022 profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/208-fiba-eurobasket/208210/players/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=18 September 2022}} The following year, Theis played a pivotal role in helping Germany capture their first world title at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 FIBA World Cup]]. He attained averages of 10.9 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game.{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis 2023 FIBA World Cup profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/201-fiba-basketball-world-cup/208182/players/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=10 September 2023}} In 2024, Theis was part of the Germany team that reached the semi-finals of the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympic Games]], where he averaged 7.8 points and seven rebounds per game.{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis 2024 Olympic Games profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/teams/germany/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=10 August 2024}} In September 2025, Theis helped Germany win their second European title all-time at [[EuroBasket 2025]], averaging 10.2 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.{{cite news|title=Daniel Theis EuroBasket 2025 profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/teams/germany/181996-daniel-theis|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=14 September 2025}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player
